newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador's army withdraws support for Bucaram.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador's army withdraws support for Bucaram.

text.p: A regional army chief said on Saturday that the miltary had withdrawn all support for President Abdala Bucaram and no longer recognized him as Ecuador's commander-in-chief.
"The armed forces have decided not to support Bucaram," Gen. Jose Grijalva, commander of the army's 7th military zone, based in the southern province of Loja, told local radio.
"We are no longer taking orders from Bucaram, since he is no longer in charge and was destituted by the National Congress," said Grijalva in an interview with Radio Centinela.

Grijalva, a respected army general who played a prominent role in Ecuador's 1995 border conflict with Peru, gave the impression that he was speaking on behalf of senior military officials across the country, but this could not be immediately confirmed.

The Quito-based military high command declined to comment earlier on Saturday on national radio reports saying the military had withdrawn all official support for Bucaram, who was voted out of office by Congress on Thursday on grounds of mental incompetence.
The reports were followed by an official annoucement that Bucaram's defense minister, Gen. Victor Bayas, had resigned.
